html:
The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland joined Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland from 1953 to 1963 under a government in Salisbury dominated by white settlers.

Supporters said it would combine the copper of the north, the labour of Nyasaland and the farms and industry of the south. It built the Kariba Dam. Africans saw it as a step toward settler rule like South Africa's and opposed it from the start.

Protests led by Banda and Kaunda made it unworkable, and Britain dissolved it at the end of 1963. Zambia and Malawi became independent in 1964, while Southern Rhodesia's whites moved toward UDI.
sum: The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland joined Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland from 1953 to 1963 under a government in Salisbury dominated by white settlers.
